chunks.text: Although the proposed approach could be considered deterministic in nature, the high variability in the illumination conditions, camera vibrations, unknown and unex- pected static or dynamic objects introduce the aforementioned uncertainty. Hence, the proposed computer vision approach deals with differences in initial conditions, belonging to a kind of systems with a chaotic deterministic behaviour in the context of applied soft computing in agricultural machinery. The experimental results show that our method is suitable and effective in the context of our agricultural scenarios. We also show that trees detection is possible from the point of view of image analysing processing, making it a useful contribution for path localization and path mapping tasks. More speciﬁcally, another important contribution is that no training process is required. It is entirely based on a combination of digital and image analysis techniques. Object detection on video sequences is still an open issue demanding special attention in view of the commercialization of these vehicles in the future. We have established an important basis 96 Y. Campos et al. / Applied Soft Computing 45 (2016) 86–97 for continuing towards ﬁnding a global solution to the problem of detecting obstacles for safe navigation in autonomous agricul- tural vehicles. For future work we propose exploring the following possibilities to improve the results hereby presented: i Results in Tables 5 and 6 suggest that OF techniques combined with our proposal can be beneﬁcial in order to discriminate between static and non-static obstacles. ii The segmentation algorithm described in Section 3.1 has been improved with temporal analysis. However, the results also show that the algorithm is not able to handle shadows, even people shadows. The process still has failures in this context; shadows are difﬁcult to identify, requiring an additional effort in this regard. iii Animals, people, cars, fence posts, trees, buildings, and so on, need to be correctly classiﬁed in order to gain maneouverability and autonomy for vehicles in the ﬁeld. iv Motion detection can be used for performing a tracking task of dynamic objects at the scene. They must be equipped with a robot navigation system for sensing, mapping, localization, path planning, and obstacle avoidance. In autonomous vehicles, safety becomes a major challenge where unexpected obstacles in the working area must be conveniently addressed. Of particular interest are, people or animals crossing in front of the vehicle or ﬁxed/moving uncatalogued elements in speciﬁc positions. Detection of unexpected obstacles or elements on video sequences acquired with a machine vision system on- board a tractor moving in cornﬁelds makes the main contribution to this research. We propose a new strategy for automatic video analysis to detect static/dynamic obstacles in agricultural environments via spatial-temporal analysis. At a ﬁrst stage obstacles are detected by using spatial information based on spectral colour analysis and texture data. At a second stage temporal information is used to detect moving objects/obstacles at the scene, which is of particular interest in camouﬂaged elements within the environment. A main feature of our method is that it does not require any training process. Another feature of our approach consists in the spatial analysis to obtain an initial segmentation of interesting objects; afterwards, temporal information is used for discriminating between moving and static objects.
